evidence.title: Test of the claim that the fountains stopped when Benoist died in 1774
evidence.summary: Result: the common form of the claim is wrong in two ways. (1) The machines failed before Benoist died: the wheel broke in 1763 and windlasses replaced it. (2) The fountains did not stop: reports of 1786 and 1789 have men filling the reservoir a day or two before a visit so that the water could play for the emperor (Bourgeois); wicker buckets from the river (Amiot); pipes repaired 1794, Dutch envoys meant to see the 水法 in early 1795 (E0185); machines scrapped 1795, but 嘉庆's poems of 1796-98 still mention water sent by machine: poetry, weak. Holding: after 1763 or so the fountains ran on occasion with stored water, carried by labour.

evidence.title: Bourgeois 1786: the fountains after Benoist
evidence.excerpt_other: un ou deux jours auparavant, on emploie tant de monde à porter l'eau que le bassin immense du château d'eau est suffisamment rempli, et les eaux jouent sur le passage de l'Empereur.
evidence.summary: Benoist's machine had worn out and was not repaired. Men filled the reservoir a day or two before the emperor's visit. Main pipes as thick as a man's body, medium and large ones of copper.

evidence.title: Engravings 11 to 13: 海晏堂 north, east and south
evidence.excerpt_other: The tallest parts of the building covered the hydraulic machines, and between them lay the reservoir.
evidence.summary: North front covers the machines, with the reservoir between; zigzag stairs at the east end lead to the reservoir; the south side repeats the north.

evidence.title: Amiot 1789: buckets from the river
evidence.excerpt_other: ils les emploient à puiser dans la rivière avec des seaux d'osier, et à porter ces eaux dans le grand réservoir qui fournit aux différents canaux,
evidence.summary: From Mémoires des missionnaires XIV p.527, quoted by Delatour. Machines ruined, eunuchs afraid of blame; wicker buckets from the river close by.

evidence.title: 刘阳, 《圆明园的故事》, excerpt on 西洋楼, 澎湃
evidence.summary: 刘阳: 海晏堂, 1759, largest of the group; behind it the water tower, an H-plan solid building with a gallery below and balconies above, and a spiral stone stair on the east.

evidence.title: 海晏堂蓄水楼 加固, 北京青年报 via 人民网
evidence.summary: The surviving water tower of 海晏堂 is a rammed-earth core like an inverted truncated pyramid, about 7.2 m high. Conservation in 2016 propped the four corners with about 160,000 bricks and added a concealed drain on top.

facts.label: Note
facts.value: S06: 东西8.55丈, 南北1.85丈, 深4.9尺 (lead). Benoist's machine out of use by 1786; reservoir filled by men with buckets; main pipes copper, as thick as a man's body (S258, pp.165-169). Round 6 replaced frontage 30.6 m. Round 6 replaced depth 27.5 m.

facts.label: Plan reader's note
facts.value: rect=128,91,0. Long rectangle x 10026-10154, y 1062-1153, with the label 海晏堂. Inner lines suggest a tank between two side corridors: probably the reservoir 锡海 (Malone: reservoir between the hydraulic machines). Label names the whole group.
